item.description:
Share usage between your accounts

A Claude can now let its Claude Code draw on your other accounts when its own allowance runs low, without signing out of anything. Add another of your Claudes under Shared usage, or sign in to an account from Graft without making a shortcut for it. Only the model's answers come from the other accounts; your chats, artifacts and connectors stay with the Claude's own account, and the Chat tab is never shared. The menu bar shows every account a Claude draws on and rings the one answering in red, and the conversation on screen runs across it with the account answering it, about a second after you switch to it. An older chat that no account has answered yet shows by its name alone, and archiving or deleting a conversation takes it off the bar. The dropdown lets you choose which account answers each conversation, with a tick beside the choice in force. Sharing needs macOS 15.

Artifacts, projects and search across accounts

Three new panes reach claude.ai for every account you sign in to there. Artifacts lists them all together: open one, copy its link, make it private or public, rename, duplicate or delete it, and export it as Markdown, PDF, a Word document or its page source. Share an artifact with a group you keep in Graft, and each person is invited as a viewer, commenter or editor. Projects lists every account's projects, and Search Chats searches every account's chats and Claude Code sessions at once, with filters for where a session ran and whether a chat is archived. Each account signs in once, with the code claude.ai emails you, in a window of Graft's; the sign-in is kept apart for that account and is never read by Graft.

A new window

The window has a proper sidebar, and every page fits at its smallest size without scrolling. Every Claude and every lent account now gets a colour of its own, so no two look alike; the Claudes you already have keep theirs.

A new Claude now starts with chats of its own, and sharing another Claude's chats is a choice you make on its page. Claudes you already have keep reading what they read before.

The Help menu now leads to the site, the release list, a new issue, and an email that already carries your Graft and macOS versions.

Accounts without a five-hour limit

Some plans now have only a weekly limit. Usage for those accounts had stopped updating, and where it did show, the five-hour figure read 0%. Graft now says an account has no five-hour limit in place of that bar, leaves out Start Session for it, and shows its weekly figure in the menu bar with a W in front, so W 94% means 94% of the week.

Pinned chats sync between profiles again with current versions of Claude, sessions from another Mac are left out of the sidebar, and Claude's updater now stays hidden and signed out while it installs.

Works on Apple Silicon and Intel, with macOS 13 or later supported.

Upgrading from 1.0.x

As with 1.1.0, shared profiles merge their chat histories on their next launch. Going back to a profile's own chats preserves what it brought, but copies already merged into the source stay there. If you need an untouched copy, back up your Claude profile folders in ~/Library/Application Support before upgrading.

See which Claude you are using

Every running Claude shows Claude's own name and icon in the Dock, so it was hard to tell which account was in front. The menu bar now shows it instead: while a Claude is in front, Graft's icon in the menu bar carries that shortcut's icon beside that account's usage. You can add its name in Settings, or turn either off.

Usage figures now say when they were taken and where they came from, and each account has its own refresh button. An open Claude's account is checked more often, bringing a Claude to the front refreshes it, and Refresh Usage now always asks for a new figure.

A conversation you edited, retried or resumed no longer shows up several times in a shared sidebar, and a chat you forked keeps both halves.

Every control now works with VoiceOver and says which account it acts on, and the Claude update line at the top takes less room.

Works on Apple Silicon and Intel, with macOS 13 or later supported.

Update when you are ready

Graft has always installed its own updates as soon as they appear. That is still the default, but you can now turn on Hold Claude Graft updates in the menu bar or in Settings. Graft keeps checking every hour and shows a new version in the menu and on its icon, but downloads nothing until you press Install. Turn the hold off and updates go back to installing themselves.

Opening a shortcut you have renamed now opens that profile. Before, Graft could fail to find the renamed shortcut and open your main Claude instead.

Works on Apple Silicon and Intel, with macOS 13 or later supported.

Your sidebar comes with you

Switching accounts shouldn't mean rebuilding your pinned list. Profiles that share Claude Code chats now keep their pins, pinned order and Code sort choice in sync. Unpin a chat in either profile and it stays unpinned in the other.

To sync the sidebar, quit the linked Claude apps, then open either shortcut. If one is still open, Graft waits until the next opening and tells you what to close. Other chats, custom groups and account settings stay as they were.

That weird transparent bar over the shortcut settings on macOS 27 is gone. The name and profile controls are clickable again. Shared profiles also keep their own permission choices, so sharing chats no longer replaces the settings you picked in Claude. Missing local MCP server definitions can still be copied over; existing server settings stay yours.

Tested with Claude Desktop 2.110.1 on macOS 27, including real restarts, two-way pin and sort changes, and clearing the last pin. Still universal for Apple Silicon and Intel, with macOS 13 or later supported.

Coming from 1.0.x?

Shared profiles merge their chat histories on the next launch. Switching back to a profile's own chats keeps what it brought, but copies already merged into the source stay there. If you want an untouched copy, back up your Claude profile folders in ~/Library/Application Support before updating.

Clearer account controls and more personal shortcuts

The Claude Desktop update bar now has its own space above the account list and profile controls. The first account and the top of each form stay visible, including in smaller windows.

Choose a colour or a Work, Personal, Code or Research icon for each shortcut to make accounts easier to tell apart. The app also includes Russian localization, including update warnings, recovery messages and account controls. Fable usage appears when the account reports a separate limit.

Updating a shortcut now prepares and verifies the replacement before changing the installed app. If preparation fails, the existing shortcut stays usable, including when the update would rename it.

Upgrading from 1.0.x

As with 1.1.0, shared profiles merge their chat histories on their next launch. Going back to a profile's own chats preserves what it brought, but copies already merged into the source stay there. If you need an untouched copy, back up your Claude profile folders in ~/Library/Application Support before upgrading.

Choose when Claude updates

Turn on Update Claude Desktop manually in Graft's menu bar or Settings to stop automatic updates from interrupting work in Claude or any of your shortcuts. The setting takes effect when each Claude next starts, so finish your work before restarting an instance that is already open.

Graft checks for Claude updates at launch and hourly, including while Claude is running. An available version appears in the window and menu bar, and the menu bar icon changes to an exclamation mark. Check for Claude Updates checks immediately.

Update Claude… warns that all running Claude instances will close and their workflows will stop. Cancel leaves them running. Confirming rechecks the release, waits for every approved instance to quit, and starts Claude's own updater. Graft shows progress and verifies the installed version before reporting success. An instance that refuses to quit is never forced closed, and one opened after confirmation requires another decision.

Manual update mode stays on during installation. Provider settings, logins, and shortcut relationships stay in place. Turning manual mode off restores the previous automatic update settings.

When Claude's automatic updater reopens the default profile instead of the shortcut you were using, Graft can now reopen the affected shortcut after installation. A profile you quit yourself stays closed. If the wrong instance has opened the same chats, Graft asks before reopening the shortcut. Workflows that Claude ended during its update still need to be resumed.

Upgrading from 1.0.x

As with 1.1.0, shared profiles merge their chat histories on their next launch. Going back to a profile's own chats preserves what it brought, but copies already merged into the source stay there. If you need an untouched copy, back up your Claude profile folders in ~/Library/Application Support before upgrading.

Sharing a history now merges it

Until now, pointing one profile at another's chats replaced its own. Your conversations went into a hidden folder beside them and the other profile's stood in their place, and a profile sharing chats this way could not archive, rename or delete any of them — Claude will not write a record into a folder that lives outside the profile.

From this version the folder is real and the two histories are merged, so both sidebars hold both sets and a shared profile behaves like a profile again.

Worth reading before you install this one

Merging cannot be undone. The first launch after updating copies each sharing profile's conversations into the profile it borrows from. Sending it back to its own chats afterwards gives back everything it started with, but the copies stay where they were merged.

Take a copy first if that matters to you. Every profile lives in ~/Library/Application Support; copying the Claude folders somewhere safe is the whole backup, and it takes a minute.

Nothing is thrown away on the way. What each profile brought to the merge is kept in a hidden folder beside its chats, which is what going back reads from. And if a conversation does go missing, it is almost always still on disk: the transcripts are in ~/.claude/projects, and Graft files a record back for any session that lost one.

This is the only update that will ask. Later ones install themselves quietly, the way they always have.
